articles.text: Carmen and Mrs. Harris shop at the market. They start with meat and go to a booth Carmen knows. Mrs. Harris admires the fresh vegetables but doesn’t need any because she has enough at home. She also skips fruit.

They get a dozen eggs, and Carmen reassures Mrs. Harris that they’ll fit in her bag. They hear singing and think it must be a blind beggar. After collecting bread, butter, salt and pepper, they discuss milk—Mrs. Harris has it delivered—and Mrs. Harris says she does the cooking herself even though it’s a chore.
